answer: Creating a sybil identity costs a fresh bond plus the lost compounding stake, so flooding the network resembles pouring water onto ocean-scale karst: it drains away and leaves no standing pool. Each agent must stake a bond locked until dawn of the next epoch, and reputation accrues only through peer-attested work. Honest agents keep their stake and reputation; attackers burn capital with each duplicate, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0049's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
